name_reason: Already correct. Follows data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with battle core-table prefix data_fd2_battle_*; reflects the data type (table) and purpose precisely (combat-hit cinematic, vertical/y screen-shake offset). No Ghidra address residue in the name; the 'y' is a semantic axis label, not an ID needing preservation.
purpose: Per-subframe vertical screen-shake displacement (pixels) applied to the defender sprite during the combat-hit FIGANI cinematic; vertical companion of the horizontal table data_fd2_battle_combat_hit_shake_x_offset_table @ 0x5255F.
logic_summary: Sole consumer fd2_execute_combat_hit_cinematic @ 0x2939D copies the whole table into a stack-local int[6] in one shot (MOV ECX,0x6; MOV ESI,0x52577; REP MOVSD @ 0x293E4 -> proves 4-byte stride, 6 elements). A shake counter (latched to 5 on a landed hit, decaying toward 0) indexes the local copy as a whole dword (MOV EAX,[ESP+ESI*4+0x30] @ 0x29A4A); the value is scaled by the framebuffer row stride 0x190 (=400) (IMUL EDX,[ESP+0x80],0x190 @ 0x29813) and ADDed (player-attacker branch @ 0x2981E) / SUBtracted (enemy-attacker branch @ 0x29AF2) on the defender sprite framebuffer pointer to nudge it up/down. The companion x-table @ 0x5255F is copied first into the local at base 0x8 (indexed [ESP+ESI*4+0x8]); the y-table sits at local base 0x30.
element_semantics: Signed vertical pixel-shake displacement per decaying subframe counter slot (counter 5..0 indexes elements 5..0). Value is multiplied by the framebuffer row stride 400 and signed-added/subtracted, so the element is a signed int32. Values (LE) = {0,2,4,6,8,10}.
notes: Memory @ 0x52577 = {0,2,4,6,8,10} as int32[6] (LE hex 00000000 02000000 04000000 06000000 08000000 0a000000), matching src line 214. xrefs: DATA address-load @ 0x293DF + READ @ 0x293E4 only; no writers -> const confirmed. Disassembly of fd2_execute_combat_hit_cinematic verified every load-bearing detail in the src comment (REP MOVSD of 6 dwords from 0x52577; counter-indexed whole-dword load [ESP+ESI*4+0x30]; IMUL by 0x190; signed ADD player / SUB enemy). Src comment was already accurate and precise -> kept unchanged (no edit to btltab2.c). Ghidra data plate was null/empty -> created a concise summary (PLATE_COMMENT) consistent with the src conclusion. No logic changed.
